functions.name: State a price and answer price questions

exponents: The price is ₹5,000, including the basic service.
That price is for one item; delivery costs extra.
The total comes to ₹5,500 with delivery.
L0|CFN-0085|B1.notes: Explain what the stated price covers and distinguish it from the final total.

L1|STM-0019.description: A customer asks about an item's price. The worker explains the quoted amount and what it includes, clarifies any known additional charges, and checks that the customer understands the total. This situation explains a price; it does not require bargaining.
flow: Identify the item or option being priced.
State the price and what it includes.
Confirm the customer's understanding of the total.
variationPoints: Unit price, package price or quotation total.
Included features and separately charged additions.
Confirmed price versus an amount awaiting confirmation.
Short A2 statements or connected B1 explanations.

L2|CM-03.summary: Support a buying decision through clear, respectful communication. Establish what the customer needs, explain relevant options and prices, respond to questions or objections, and confirm the customer's choice. Distinguish available offers from requests that need authorisation. Good selling helps the customer understand the options and next step without pressure or unsupported claims.

communicationMoves.move: Welcome the customer and open the exchange.
Ask questions to understand the customer's needs.
Describe and compare relevant options.
Explain the price and respond to concerns.
Discuss an available alternative or offer within the worker's authority.
Confirm the customer's chosen option and close respectfully.
Follow up on an earlier enquiry when appropriate.

qualityCriteria: Recommendations respond to the customer's stated needs.
Prices and included items are explained clearly.
Claims are supported by available information.
The customer can decline without pressure.
The chosen option and next step are understood.

responsibilities: Welcome the customer and discover their needs.
Describe relevant options and recommend a suitable choice.
Explain the stated price and what is included.
Respond to questions or objections using available information.
Discuss terms only within the worker's authority.
Confirm the customer's decision and agreed next step.
Follow up on an enquiry or quotation respectfully.
Acknowledge complaints and involve an appropriate colleague when needed.

jobKnowledge.title: Customer requirements
jobKnowledge.text: A recommendation is stronger when it follows the customer's stated purpose, preferences and constraints. Questions gather that information before the worker describes an option.

jobKnowledge.title: Quoted information
jobKnowledge.text: A quoted price and the final amount may differ when the customer changes the option or adds something. Explain what the current quotation covers rather than treating every amount as final.

jobKnowledge.title: Authority limits
jobKnowledge.text: A sales worker may need confirmation from a colleague before agreeing a request. English can clearly distinguish a confirmed offer from a proposal awaiting a decision.

jobKnowledge.title: Follow-up purpose
jobKnowledge.text: A useful follow-up refers to a previous enquiry and asks what the customer needs next. It does not assume that silence means agreement or that a purchase decision has been made.

jobKnowledge.title: Concern versus complaint
jobKnowledge.text: A concern before purchase may require an explanation or comparison. A complaint about an earlier exchange may require fact-checking and support from another team.

responsibilities: Clarify the customer's preferred vehicle model or version.
Compare relevant vehicle features from the available product information.
Explain what the selected vehicle quotation includes and what remains to be confirmed.
Arrange the customer's test-drive appointment and confirm the meeting details.
Ask permission before proceeding with an appointment-related action.
Follow up on a showroom visit or vehicle quotation with the customer's current questions.

jobKnowledge.title: Model and version
jobKnowledge.text: A model may be offered in more than one version. Features discussed with the customer should correspond to the actual option under consideration, using the dealership's available information.

jobKnowledge.title: Vehicle quotation
jobKnowledge.text: A vehicle quotation may show several components or optional additions. Explain only the information provided in the quotation and identify amounts awaiting confirmation, without offering finance or regulatory advice.

jobKnowledge.title: Appointment coordination
jobKnowledge.text: The pilot's test-drive communication covers the preferred option, availability, timing, meeting details and related customer questions. It does not cover vehicle operation or safety training.

jobKnowledge.title: Customer choice
jobKnowledge.text: A customer may compare options, request more information or postpone a decision. The worker can clarify that preference and agree on the next contact without claiming that an appointment commits the customer to buy.

The dealership's test-drive policy, referred to generically.
The level of language support, while keeping every version communication-only.

brief.title: Following up after a quotation or visit — Car Sales Executive (B1)

exponents: I am following up on the quotation I sent yesterday.
Have you had a chance to look at the options?
We agreed to speak today; is this still a good time?
L0|CFN-0022|B1.notes: Refer to the earlier contact and invite a response without pressuring the other person.

L1|STM-0028.description: A worker contacts a customer after a quotation or visit. They refer to the earlier exchange, check whether it is a suitable time to follow up, invite questions or a decision, and establish the next contact without applying pressure.
flow: Refer to the earlier quotation or visit.
Check whether the customer can discuss it now.
Invite a response or questions about the earlier information.
Confirm the next contact or close respectfully.
variationPoints: Spoken follow-up versus a written message.
The time elapsed since the original contact.
Whether the customer wants clarification, more time or no further contact.
Brief B1 questions or more developed follow-up language.

policies.D-U11: Job knowledge only to make communication realistic; not certification. No invented safety instructions, public procedures or legal/medical/financial advice. Factual claims in regulated areas must be traceable; U-1 avoids them.
policies.D-U12: Hybrid characters: role-specific realistic characters and reusable stakeholder archetypes; no single permanent character; Arif is not used.
policies.D-U14: Learning cycle for new role content: Context → Notice → Understand → Guided Practice → Role Practice → Performance Task → Feedback → Review/Retrieval. Not claimed to exist in the current book.
policies.D-U07: Vocabulary: propose terms only; the repository assigns V-<SCOPE>-<NUMBER> codes and reuses existing codes. Never invent codes.
policies.D-U10: Generate only the requested delta. Do not regenerate objects supplied in context.

style.currency: Indian rupees (₹) unless the situation requires otherwise
style.names: realistic South Asian names by default; international names where the context has them; no stereotypes
style.brands: no real company or brand names; use generic descriptions (e.g. 'the delivery app', 'the dealership')
style.languages: English only. No Bengali or Hindi script or transliteration in U-1.
style.audio: None. Content must be fully usable as text (D-U06).

context.review: Output is stored as GENERATED, then AI QA, then Editorial Review by the author. Specialist and native review are NOT_REQUIRED for U-1. It is never published.

instructions: Return ONE JSON object only (no prose, no Markdown fences), conforming to the response format in 'responseFormat'.
Produce exactly the outputs listed in 'expectedOutputs', using their tempId, type and key unchanged.
Generate only these outputs. Do not regenerate objects given in 'context' — use them.
Do not invent IDs or vocabulary codes. Reference existing codes only as given in context; propose new vocabulary with tempIds.
English only: no Bengali/Hindi script or transliteration. No audio references. No real brand or company names.
No legal, medical, financial or safety advice; no invented procedures or rules (D-U11).
Report honestly in selfCheck: 'met', 'not met' or 'uncertain'. Never claim approval, certification or CEFR validation.
